clue.text: Keep watch on lamb half burnt by Mary

indicators.note: in a down-the-page reading, one piece placed on another comes after it, so the timer follows
only the first half of the word lamb is wanted here

parts.note: a timer is a device that keeps watch on the passing minutes

explanation.surface: Someone is told to guard a lamb that has been half cooked by a woman called Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the timer after LA, the first half of 'lamb'. 'Mary' is Queen Mary I, under whom the Protestant bishop was burnt at the stake in 1555.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Latimer, Bishop of Worcester, was a Protestant martyr executed at Oxford in Queen Mary I's reign.

clue.text: Natural ability to find solutions

explanation.definitionFit: One's lights are one's mental gifts, as in by their lights; in crosswords, lights are the answers entered in the grid.

clue.text: Cross, having to glean after threshing

indicators.note: threshing beats the crop, so the letters of to glean are knocked about

explanation.surface: Someone is angry at having to gather leftover grain after the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' seems to mean angry; it is a hybrid fruit. 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a hybrid between a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Diana's light nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman moon goddess, so her light shines from the moon; moonshine also means foolish talk.

clue.text: Impressive bid to capture sleeping bat

indicators.note: the bridge call holds the turned animal inside it

parts.note: redouble is a call in the card game bridge

indicators.note: a bat sleeps hanging upside down, so the word is turned over

explanation.surface: A remarkable offer is made to catch a dozing bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeping' is the reversal signal because bats sleep hanging upside down; 'to capture' puts the turned animal inside a call from the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubtable means formidable, commanding respect.

clue.text: Would one lie on this? Well, no

definitions.text: Would one lie on this? Well, no

parts.words: Would one lie on this? Well, no
parts.note: the place one lies when not well, that is when ill; the surface reads as a query about telling untruths

explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' looks like telling an untruth and 'Well, no' like a hesitant reply, but it means lying down when not well.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who is ill lies in a bed set aside for convalescence.

clue.text: Desire to be title-holder

indicators.note: the word desire is the holder, containing the letters of the title

explanation.surface: Someone longs to become a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'title-holder' reads as a champion, but 'Desire' holds the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the honorific given to a knight or baronet.

clue.text: Starts to complain about violence in London — trivial complaint

indicators.note: the opening letters of the five words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: Someone begins grumbling about street violence in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavil is a petty objection.

clue.text: Original theory created by 9 or 21?

parts.note: the cosmological theory of how the universe began, jokingly put down to an explosive or a surprise from two other entries

explanation.walkthrough: 9 and 21 refer to the entries for the explosive and the surprise, each of which would make a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The theory says the universe originated from a single explosive expansion.

clue.text: Holding up fish, gripping tail with difficulty

indicators.note: the fish holds the rearranged word inside it

parts.note: the dory is a sea fish

indicators.note: the letters of tail are got out awkwardly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A fisherman is held up landing a fish whose tail he struggles to grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' is the anagram signal on 'tail', and 'gripping' puts the result inside the fish; 'Holding up' means delaying, not supporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means slow and delaying.

clue.text: Plot producing green tea?

parts.note: a plot of land growing tea, which actually points to a famous 1605 conspiracy's explosive and to a Chinese tea with rolled pellet-like leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a garden plot growing tea; it is the 1605 Plot to blow up Parliament, and the same name is used for a Chinese green tea rolled into pellets.
explanation.definitionFit: The explosive of Guy Fawkes's 1605 conspiracy shares its name with a pellet-rolled Chinese green tea.

clue.text: Watch classical poet right out of sight

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken away so it can no longer be seen

parts.note: Virgil, the Roman poet of the Aeneid

explanation.surface: A guard keeps watch over an ancient poet, the right one, until he vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep watch, as over a sick person.

clue.text: Anguish — girl's lost some hair

indicators.note: the girl's name and its s are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: distress is anguish
Di is a girl's name, with the 's adding S

explanation.surface: In her anguish a girl has had some of her hair cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl's' gives DI plus the S of the possessive, three letters taken from the front of DISTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of a person's hair.

clue.text: A continental lover found discourteous

parts.note: un is French for a, so a continental a
a gallant is a lover or suitor

explanation.surface: A European suitor turns out to be rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' signals a word from mainland Europe: French UN for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the courtesy towards women expected of a chivalrous man is rude behaviour.

clue.text: Jumbo jets heard east of the Rockies

parts.note: jumbo means huge

indicators.note: the word for jets is said aloud, giving a word for flat land

parts.note: jet aircraft

explanation.surface: Large jet aircraft can be heard on the eastern side of the Rockies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo jets' looks like one phrase, but Jumbo gives GREAT and jets give planes, which sound like PLAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast prairie region of North America lies east of the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Would this creature keep the others out of Nativity scene?

definitions.text: Would this creature keep the others out of Nativity scene?

parts.words: Would this creature keep the others out of Nativity scene?
parts.note: an animal lying in the crib of the Bethlehem stable and refusing to let anyone else near, which is the fable of a spiteful hoarder

explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop's fable a dog lies in a manger of hay it cannot eat and stops the oxen eating; the clue pictures it in the Christmas stable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a spiteful person who keeps others from something they cannot use themselves, after Aesop's fable.

clue.text: Did she train as a sob-sister?

definitions.text: Did she train as a sob-sister?

parts.words: Did she train as a sob-sister?
parts.note: a woman who writes a newspaper problem page, as if she had qualified in sorrow

explanation.walkthrough: A sob sister was a journalist who wrote sentimental stories; the clue asks if a writer of advice columns trained for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a columnist answers readers' letters about personal troubles in a magazine.

clue.text: He doesn't strike poet as one receptive to points

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A man who refuses to hit a poet is said to be open to argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a blow, but it is industrial action; 'points' are the tips of swords.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath that receives the point of a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Managed to secure each base with full guarantees

indicators.note: the word for managed holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: coped means managed
per means each, as in a pound per head
bottom means base

explanation.surface: Someone has managed to make every base safe with full guarantees.
explanation.definitionFit: Something copper-bottomed is thoroughly reliable, like a ship sheathed in copper below the waterline.

clue.text: Fish-cake from Yorkshire captivated King Richard

explanation.definitionFit: Pomfret is a sea fish and a liquorice cake from Pontefract in Yorkshire; Pontefract, also called Pomfret, castle held King Richard II captive.

clue.text: Take to one's heart new places when travelling

indicators.note: travelling moves the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone warmly embraces new places on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclasp is to hold in an embrace.

clue.text: "The street Wren built" is to be broadcast

indicators.note: the letters of Wren are built into a new structure

explanation.surface: A street designed by the architect Christopher Wren is to be on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' seems to mean transmitted; it means scattered, as seed is sown. 'built' rearranges WREN into REWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered widely, as a farmer scatters seed by hand.

clue.text: With a lot of money, she will create a big surprise

parts.note: a bomb is British slang for a large sum, as in costing a bomb
she'll, contracted

explanation.surface: A woman with plenty of cash is going to cause a great shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cost a bomb' is British slang for costing a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a shocking piece of news that comes out of the blue.

clue.text: Welsh swimmer is new to breakers

indicators.note: the words is new are handed over to be broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Welsh swimmer is a novice in the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakers' looks like surf; it means the letters of IS NEW are broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: The sewin is the Welsh name for the sea trout, a fish.

clue.text: Got rhyme for 'craft'

indicators.note: the clue tells you a word that rhymes with the answer

parts.note: the word got, which rhymes with a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone has found a rhyme for the word craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got' and the boat end in the same sound, despite the odd spelling of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or pleasure boat, and craft means a vessel.

clue.text: School head mislaid pointer

indicators.note: the first letter of the school's name is lost

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.surface: A headmaster has lost his pointer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School head' looks like a headmaster, but 'head mislaid' drops the H from HARROW, an English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign used to point the way.

clue.text: Insist on turning up — it's after time

indicators.note: the words up and it's are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: it's taken as written, without the apostrophe
late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone demands that you show up, as it is already late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses 'up it's' to give STIPU, then LATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to demand something as a condition of an agreement.

clue.text: Girl unable to finish pudding

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for pudding is not reached

parts.note: suet is a short name for a suet pudding, a steamed British dessert

explanation.surface: A girl cannot finish her dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Cooling off wine in the river

indicators.note: the wine goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee, a river in Wales, England and Scotland
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Bottles of wine are put to cool in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is an old name for a red wine from Spain, often used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Detente is an easing of tension between nations, a relaxing of hostility.

clue.text: Check behind

explanation.definitionFit: To sit upon something is to suppress or check it; a sit-upon is a jocular word for the buttocks.
